one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window: Q2 FY27 is set for 2026-12-14. Events inside it: (1) the $0.50 dividend (record Oct 9, paid Oct 23; ~0.35% ex-div drag) [1]; (2) an Oracle investor day that management flagged on the Q1 call for October. The date is unconfirmed, but last year's analyst meeting was held at AI World and AI World 2026 runs Oct 25-28 [2,45,46]. It is two-sided: it could give an FCF-positive date, AI-infrastructure margins and FY28 capex, or another capex step-up; (3) Big-4 Q3 results with first 2027 capex guides (~Oct 28-29) and the FOMC (Oct 27-28). Strong hyperscaler capex helps demand sentiment but revives the financing worry, so I take no directional view. I use a lognormal centred just under spot (median ~$142.9 after the dividend) with monthly sigma ~16.5%, slightly above 56%/3.5 = 16.0% for the guidance event.

fair_value.method: 60/40 blend of P/E (CY2028 EPS $12.34 x 14.5x = $179) and EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA ~$61.4B x 10.5x = $645B EV, less ~$150B net debt + preferred excluding operating leases, over ~3.10B shares = $160) -> ~$171. The ~33% P/E discount to the 21.65x peer median is held constant, not closed.

inputs_detail.derivation: Yahoo consensus $11.00 (39 analysts, range $9.00-13.30), haircut ~5% for falling OCI gross margin during the ramp, rising interest and depreciation, and dilution from the remaining ~$20-40B of FY27 financing due Jan-May 2027.

FY28 $10.5 x 1.30. Management's reconfirmed 28% EPS CAGR to FY30 gives x1.28; the Zacks FY29/FY28 ratio is 12.84/9.14 = 1.40 (only 5 estimates, GAAP-like basis), implying ~$15.4 non-GAAP. I take 1.30, nearer management's pace, so I stay ~11% below the consensus-implied figure.

inputs_detail.input: CY2028 EPS (next calendar year at the Oct-2027 horizon)
inputs_detail.derivation: 5/12 x 10.5 + 7/12 x 13.65 = 12.34. This matches the peer basis: at Oct-2026 peers and ORCL are measured on CY2027, so at Oct-2027 the same lag is CY2028. For reference, the 12-month NTM at Oct-2027 (8/12 FY28 + 4/12 FY29) is $11.55.

Peer CY2027 median is 21.65x (n=10, range 8.5-27.0x; hyperscalers ~23.7x, enterprise software ~15.6x). ORCL is at 14.6x today, 33% below the median. I hold the discount at ~33% through Oct-2027 because its causes persist over the horizon: FCF stays negative through FY28 peak capex, BBB-/Baa2 against A-or-better peers, ~half of RPO is OpenAI, and the non-GAAP/GAAP gap is ~23%. 14.5x sits inside the range, between IBM (16.7x) and CRM/WDAY (14.2-14.3x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$61.4B x 10.5x = $645B; less ~$150B net debt incl. finance leases and preferred (operating leases excluded); / ~3.10B shares

inputs_detail.input: Current net debt (notes less cash and securities)
inputs_detail.derivation: Notes $7.625B + $117.712B = $125.3B, less cash $36.369B and securities $0.708B. Operating leases ($30.6B non-current) are excluded because Oracle's EBITDA is after rent.

$88.2B + Q2-Q4 FY27 FOCF ~-$36.6B (S&P FY27 -$42B less Q1 -$5.4B) + Q1 FY28 ~-$8B + dividends ~$6B + finance leases ~$9-10B + Series D preferred $5B as debt-like = ~$153B, less ~$5-10B of the 2027 raise taken as equity. This is ~$10B above the supervisor's ~$140B because I include the preferred and use S&P's FOCF.

NTM revenue = 8/12 x FY28 consensus $131.7B + 4/12 x FY29 ~$165B (+25%, judgment) = ~$142.8B, at a ~43% EBITDA margin (TTM ~48%, diluted by lower-margin GPU IaaS). Round 1 used CY28 revenue (~$151B) for a figure labelled NTM, now corrected.

ORCL today is ~11x NTM EBITDA (EV ~$530B ex operating leases / ~$47B). Peer forward median ~14.5x is approximate and mixed-basis, so it is context only. The range runs from CRWV ~5.8x to NOW ~33x. Capex intensity (FY27 gross capex $90-95B vs ~$45B EBITDA) means EBITDA overstates owner earnings, so I hold near today's level, inside the range.
3,023.7M outstanding on 2026-09-07 + dilution/RSUs + ~$5-10B equity in 2027 at ~$150.

bear.story: OpenAI (about half of RPO, ~$60B/yr from FY28) slows or renegotiates Stargate take-up. Site delays like Jupiter (force majeure, $18B loan ~90c) spread. The Jan-May 2027 raise prices on distressed terms, and Moody's cuts to Baa3 with S&P pressure building. FY28 EPS falls to ~$8.5-9 and the market pays ~10x CY28 EPS of ~$9.5.

base.story: OCI converts backlog (RPO $664B, GPU utilisation ~98%, renewal pricing +20%). The FY27 guide (>=$90B revenue, $8.10 EPS) is met, the 2027 financing gets done at BBB-/Baa2 and the June 2027 FY28 guide is near consensus. The multiple stays depressed at ~13x CY28 EPS of ~$12.3, with FCF still negative.

bull.story: OpenAI's ~$70B run-rate (Axios/Bloomberg, Sacra) and its $122B raise remove counterparty fear. Hyperscaler 2027 guides confirm demand, and the investor day or FY28 guide gives an FCF-positive date as the prepay/BYO-hardware model caps net capex. CDS tighten and the stock re-rates to ~18-19x CY28 EPS of ~$12.8.

comps_summary.peer_range: P/E is on one basis: calendar-2027 consensus non-GAAP EPS, with fiscal years calendarised (MSFT 1/2 FY27 + 1/2 FY28; CRM and WDAY FY ending Jan-28; ADBE FY Nov-27; SAP USD CY27 $9.60 from Nasdaq/Zacks, replacing round 1's StockAnalysis 'Forward PE'/1.15 conversion, which mixed fiscal years). Range 8.5x (ADBE) to 27.0x (NOW), n=10; CRWV is excluded as loss-making. Sub-medians: hyperscalers ~23.7x, enterprise software ~15.6x. Forward EV/EBITDA is ~5.8x (CRWV) to ~33x (NOW), n=11. These are my approximate derivations (TTM less ~1y growth), not one consistent consensus basis, so they are context only.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: ORCL is at 14.6x CY27 consensus ($9.81) and ~11x NTM EBITDA. I apply 14.5x CY28 EPS (33% below the 21.65x median, inside the range near IBM/CRM/WDAY) and 10.5x NTM EBITDA (inside the range, below the approximate median).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is held constant rather than widened or closed, because each of its causes runs through Oct-2027 on company facts. (1) Cash: management calls FY27-28 the peak capex years with no FCF-positive date. S&P sees FY27 FOCF ~-$42B, so FCF stays negative through May 2028, while peers fund capex from operating cash. (2) Credit: S&P BBB- (stable since Jul 9, 2026) and Moody's Baa2 negative, with ~$20-40B of financing due Jan-May 2027; every hyperscaler peer is A or better. (3) Concentration: ~half of the $664B RPO is OpenAI (per S&P), a loss-making counterparty despite its $122B raise. (4) Earnings quality: non-GAAP EPS is ~23% above GAAP (Q1 $1.92 vs $1.56), while the hyperscaler half reports near GAAP. Against that, ORCL has the fastest EPS growth in the set (~+35% FY28), which is why I do not go deeper (e.g. to ADBE's 8.5x). Closing the gap needs FCF visibility, which is the bull scenario, not the base case.

thesis_break_reason: A sustained move below ~$105 (8% under the $114.50 52-week low, about 10.7x CY27 consensus EPS) would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility. Triggers: OpenAI deferring or renegotiating its ~$300B commitment; the Jan-May 2027 raise done on distressed terms or a Moody's cut followed by S&P negative watch; or force-majeure delays spreading beyond Jupiter so that FY28 revenue lands well under ~$115B. S&P's outlook is stable, not negative as I said in round 1, so a junk downgrade within 12 months is less likely. I still keep $105 rather than the supervisor's $100 because $105 is already below the level that consensus earnings can support without backlog impairment.

reasoning: Price $143.41, down 51% in a year, 56% realised vol. Primary data, verified this round from the Q1 FY27 8-K and 10-Q: revenue $19.3B +30%, OCI $7.4B +121%, non-GAAP EPS $1.92 (GAAP $1.56), RPO $664B, OCF $23.1B, capex $28.5B, FCF -$5.4B. Notes are $125.3B and cash plus securities $37.1B, so net debt is $88.2B before leases. The ATM raised $19.9B and 3,023.7M shares were outstanding on Sep 7. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, each verified: (1) S&P's Jul 9 cut to BBB- came with a STABLE outlook (LiveSquawk headline of the S&P release, heise); Moody's Baa2 is the negative one. This trims the credit left tail. (2) My round-1 net debt (~$160B) came from stockanalysis 'debt', which includes $30.6B of non-current operating leases. Oracle's EBITDA is after rent, so that double-counted; I now use notes plus finance leases plus preferred, ~$150B at the horizon. (3) The OpenAI ~$70B run-rate is now second-sourced (Axios via Bloomberg, Sep 29), and OpenAI closed a $122B raise. Both support a smaller bear weight, but the ratio of commitments to revenue is still extreme, so I trimmed the bear weight only from 27% to 25%. (4) The investor day in October and Q2 on Dec 14 go into the catalysts and the 1-month view. Valuation: Zacks FY29/FY28 = 1.40 (verified) implies non-GAAP FY29 ~$15.4. I use $13.65 (x1.30 on my $10.5 FY28) for CY28 EPS of $12.34. On a single CY27 basis, peers have a median of 21.65x; ORCL is at 14.6x (-33%), and I hold that discount for the reasons in comps_summary: P/E leg 14.5x -> $179. The EV/EBITDA leg now uses true NTM EBITDA (~$61B, corrected from a CY28-based figure) at 10.5x -> $160. FV ~$171 (60/40). The supervisor's ~$173 for me was not copied: the NTM fix and the preferred offset the lease fix. Scenarios (medians): bear $92 / base $160 / bull $240 at 25/50/25. The weighted median price is $163, and the lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.45/0.28/0.27) has a mean of ~$171 that reconciles with FV. Total log-dispersion ~0.47 is a little under the post-crash realised 56%; the bear component carries the fat left tail. The ladder median is ~$162 and P(>=spot) ~0.61, up from 0.58: the corrections (stable S&P, lease double-count, second-sourced OpenAI revenue) are net positive. Sell-side average PT $238 was not used as an anchor.
